rounds.text: The core of the bull case rests on a significant inflection point in operational efficiency, evidenced by a massive 500% year-over-year surge in net profit [E51]. This performance is not merely accounting noise, as the company achieved a robust cash conversion ratio of 59.30x, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by actual operating cash flow [E30]. Furthermore, the company is demonstrating superior capital efficiency compared to its peers, with an ROCE of 8.78% outperforming the sector benchmark of 5.62% [E10]. While the market remains fixated on historical stagnation, the business is currently exhibiting accelerating earnings growth [E53]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with low historical ROE [E26, E27, E28], declining promoter holdings [E34, E49], and a valuation that appears rich by traditional metrics [E1, E56]. Nevertheless, the current disconnect between the improving results score of 76/100 and the prevailing cautious sentiment suggests that the market may be relying on stale data rather than the recent turnaround [E57].

India Home Loans Ltd exhibits a severe valuation disconnect, trading at an extreme trailing P/E of 303x and a sector-dwarfing 297.8x against a sector benchmark of 18.73x [E1, E6]. This pricing assumes aggressive performance that the fundamental record entirely fails to support, with a reverse DCF showing the current price of Rs 29.7 demands 47.2% earnings growth while the intrinsic DCF model pegs value at a mere Rs 1 per share [E37, E39]. Fundamental profitability and returns are chronically depressed, evidenced by a 10-year median ROE of just 3%, a 3-year median ROE of -2%, and a low trailing return on equity of 2% [E26, E28, E29, E54]. The underlying top line is in a prolonged structural contraction, highlighted by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -14%, a 3-year contraction of -13%, and trailing twelve-month sales growth of -11% [E15, E16, E17, E46]. Insider confidence is actively deteriorating alongside operational stagnation, marked by promoters slashing their holdings from 36.55% in Dec 2023 to 27.63% in Sep 2026, alongside an institutional exodus where domestic institutions cut their stake from 24.57% to a negligible 0.07% over the same period [E34, E35, E47, E49]. Conceded: the company demonstrates healthy short-term cash generation with March 2026 operating and free cash flows reaching Rs 5.93 Cr backed by a 59.30x cash conversion ratio, alongside a positive YoY net profit surge [E30, E31, E32, E51].

Conceded: promoter and domestic institutional holdings have decreased, and historical multi-year sales growth figures are negative [E15, E16, E17, E34, E35]. However, dismissing the business on trailing P/E multiples [E1, E6] ignores an active, explosive operational turnaround where net profit has surged +500% year-over-year with accelerating earnings growth [E51, E53, E57]. Conceded: the DCF model suggests overvaluation [E37, E55]. Yet, this static model completely overlooks actual incoming cash realities, where the business generated robust operating and free cash flows of Rs 5.93 Cr in March 2026 backed by an extraordinary 59.30x cash conversion ratio that proves profits are fully cash-backed [E30, E31, E32]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a very modest 1.02x price-to-book value [E2], aligning closely with the sector benchmark [E7], while delivering an ROCE of 8.78% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 5.62% [E10]. Finally, stale historical sentiment should not overshadow current results scoring 76 out of 100 on the results framework, driven by 3-year compounded profit growth of 12% [E20, E57].

Conceded: the company generated operating and free cash flows of Rs 5.93 Cr in March 2026 with a 59.30x cash conversion ratio [E30, E31, E32]. However, framing an explosive operational turnaround around a +500% net profit surge [E51, E57] ignores that 10-year compounded profit growth sits entirely flat at 0% and trailing twelve-month profit growth has plunged by -26% [E18, E21]. The bull relies on a 3-year profit growth of 12% [E20, E57], but this completely masks severe multi-year sales contraction, including a -14% drop over 5 years and an 11% decline over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Furthermore, dismissing the DCF model's warning [E37, E55] is dangerous when today's price already forces investors to price in an aggressive 47.2% earnings growth expectation against a base case of 0.0% [E39]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 8.78% [E10] and the stock trades at 1.02x book value [E2], but these metrics do not override a paltry 0.23% ROE, a miserable 2% median return on equity last year, and a low interest coverage ratio [E9, E29, E45]. Finally, citing a results score of 76/100 [E57] cannot whitewash the catastrophic flight of institutional capital, as domestic institutions slashed their holdings from 24.57% in December 2023 to a mere 0.07% by September 2026 [E35].
